gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured switchover time next to a measured PSU hold-up time. StorageReview measured the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus at just over 8 ms and the BLUETTI Elite 300 at 8 ms. It also measured older stations running slower than their ratings: the EcoFlow DELTA 2 at about 38.5 ms against a claim of under 30 ms, and the Anker SOLIX F2000 at about 27.4 ms against a 20 ms claim. On the PC side, HWBusters measured a Cooler Master Elite Gold 850W gaming PSU's hold-up at 15.6 ms, and Cybenetics measured an XPG KYBER 850 at 15.8 ms hold-up and 14.1 ms from AC loss to PWR_OK. So a station rated 15 to 20 ms leaves no margin for a typical gaming PSU, while one measured near 8 ms does.
standout_why: ChatGPT's results list for this chat is empty, so there were no cited rival pages to compare against. Its own answer labels its 0/4/10/20/30 ms switchover figures as 'Illustrative specifications, not measured performance'. It gives no PSU hold-up figure from any lab and never notes that measured switchover can be slower than the rating. Our current page already has the StorageReview 8 ms figures and a generic '16 ms PSU' note. What it lacks is a named lab's measured hold-up and PWR_OK times for actual 850 W gaming PSUs.
decides: Confirms the pick. Stations with a 10 ms or faster rating and a measured switchover near 8 ms (EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, BLUETTI Elite 300) fit inside both the measured 14.1 to 15.8 ms gaming-PSU windows and ATX 3.1's 12 ms full-load floor. Stations rated 15 to 20 ms (BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, BLUETTI AC180, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2) are at or past the 14.1 ms PWR_OK window. StorageReview's DELTA 2 and F2000 results show measured switchover can exceed the rating by 7 to 9 ms, so a 20 ms rating should not be trusted for a gaming PC.

A measured switchover test with a gaming PC under GPU load and a named PSU: the StorageReview tests used workstations or servers at unstated or idle loads, and APH did not state the PC's PSU or load.
Hold-up times measured at 115 V: the Cybenetics and HWBusters pages I opened don't say which input voltage the hold-up test used.
